title: ARIA tabs need an accessible name
summary: An element with role tab has no accessible name, so people cannot tell tabs apart. Add visible text or an aria-label.
problem: An element with role="tab" has no accessible name. This often happens when a tab holds only an icon. A screen reader announces the role and position but not what the tab shows.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear a row of tabs with no way to tell them apart. Voice control users cannot name a tab to select it.
steps: Find the tab in the scan result.
Put visible text in each tab. This is the best fix for everyone.
If a tab must be icon-only, add aria-label with a short name and set aria-hidden="true" on the icon.
Check that every tab in the tablist has a distinct name.

whyItMatters: Tabs that cannot be told apart make tabbed content unusable for people who rely on names. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Select each tab in your browser's accessibility inspector and check its Name. A screen reader should announce each tab by name.
